correctness.rationale: The substitution yields s_n=(-1)^nu2(n+1). Periodic truncation modulo 2^K differs only on at most three exceptional residue classes, so ordinary-time limits equal Haar averages on Z2. For three positions the ultrametric valuations are necessarily (m,m,t); splitting Haar U by nu2(U)<m and the two residue classes mod 2^(m+1) reduces the triple to a mean 1/3 and a pair moment at valuation t-m-1, giving 1/3-4(-1)^m/(3*2^t). Walsh expansion gives all probabilities, while t>=m+1 yields exact zero/min/max classes. Independently generated 2^15 substitution signs from recursion and checked ten triple averages against analytic values with strict finite-modulus error ≤6/32768; the infinite claim is supported by the Haar case proof.
